newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY FUTURES FOCUS ON RISING YEN, BUBOR RATE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY FUTURES FOCUS ON RISING YEN, BUBOR RATE.

text.p: The surging yen and the rising three-month Budapest Interbank Offered Rate (BUBOR) dominated Hungary's futures markets on Tuesday, dealers said.
In the Budapest Commodity Exchange's currency futures section, turnover totalled 5.94 billion forints, or 28,462 lots.
BUBOR futures traded in an unusually high turnover, in 4,306 lots.
BCE dealers said that interest in BUBOR futures, which trade under favourable conditions compared with currencies, strengthened much recently.
"The interest of banks in three-month BUBOR futures is increasing," said Janos Szolyka of Swap Broker.
He added that expectations of how inflation and interest rates would change this year, were mixed and this encouraged speculation in BUBOR futures.
Yen deals accounted for more than half of the BCE's foreign currency futures turnover on Tuesday.

"The yen's overnight strengthening by one forint on the spot market has attracted the interest of speculants and individuals," Szolyka said, adding that many players expected that the yen's firming to be reversed for the longer term.
For the most busy December maturity, the yen (100 units) rose 60 fillers to 162.10 forints.
The sterling, if it remains strong on international markets, is likely to attract strong interest on Wednesday, dealers said.
Currency futures trade on the Budapest Stock Exchange was slow.
The yen (100 units) was fixed by the National Bank of Hungary at 145.13 forints on Tuesday, up from 143.96 on Monday. The sterling was fixed at 295.40 forints, up from 295.30.
